messages:
dina: Heads-up: CI microbench failed on PR #1987 (batch_scheduler + quantization changes). Seems like a perf threshold diff.

ci-bot: [PERF][FAIL] microbench batch_scheduler_throughput exceeded threshold.
Link: https://ci.internal/runs/98765

```
metric: median_latency_ms
baseline: 12.10
PR: 13.45
delta: +1.35 (11.2%)
kv_hit_rate: 0.824 -> 0.703 (-14.7%)
```

ben: Reproduced locally on `ci-gpu-rtx6000`. Running `./tools/microbench --suite=batch_scheduler --runs=50` gives similar numbers.

alice: Profiled a few traces; flamegraph points to kernel_selector::choose_for_quantized and setup cost in fused_quant_kernel.cpp. Small batches (<=4) now pick fused kernel with higher init latency.

eli: Candidate commits between good..bad: `a7f3d2b` (batch scheduler tweak), `b9c1fae` (quant kernel autoselect change). My hunch is b9c1fae.

ben: Quick local bisect narrowed to `b9c1fae` — toggling `USE_FUSED_QUANT_KERNS=0` removes the regression.

dina: OK plan: temporary revert of `b9c1fae` on PR branch to unblock rollout. Then follow up: rework kernel autoselect to consider small-batch latency.

ben: I'll open revert PR in 15m and run the full microbench suite.

ci-bot: [INFO] new run started: https://ci.internal/runs/98792

alice: Short-term mitigation: set `REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR_PREFER_FUSED=false` in canary config to avoid picking fused path.

eli: I'll do the canary config update once revert PR is merged.

dina: Agreed. Hold merges touching kernel selector until we have a perf fix. Thanks all :thumbsup:
